# Where AI might plug in

## My view {.center}

::: {style="font-size: 1.25em; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
Many of these approaches are under-explored and not well integrated with
the rapidly evolving, noisy, sparse data settings I have worked in.
I am not aware of any real-world operational use so far, and I am mostly
not convinced by the evaluations of proposed methods.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em; margin-top: 1em; color: #4a5899;"}
Sam Abbott, September 2026
:::

::: {.fragment style="font-size: 1.6em; margin-top: 1.2em;"}
And yet. I am very excited about their potential.
:::

## A neural network as a component?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
- **Universal differential equations (UDEs) and physics-informed neural
  networks (PINNs).** A network inside a mechanistic model. Here the
  mechanism is the renewal process
- **A network in the $R_t$ slot.** It learns what the autoregressive
  (AR) process cannot say. Behaviour, season, policy
- **A network on the observation side.** Several data streams fitted
  from the same latent infections
- Most exciting where there are many hard to model data sets to fit
  jointly in an otherwise well understood system
- No neural network code in any EpiAware package yet

::: {.attribution}
Rackauckas et al. 2020,
[arXiv:2001.04385](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04385) ·
Millevoi, Pasetto and Ferronato 2024, PLoS Comput Biol ·
Philipps, Schmid and Hasenauer 2025, npj Syst Biol Appl ·
grep of the EpiAware organisation for Lux and Flux, 2026-09-11
:::
:::

## Renewal processes as a neural network layer

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A specialised form of PINN
- A renewal process is an autoregressive transformation of $R_t$ and
  past infections to today's infections
- It can be thought of as a neural network layer
- Stacked with other layers. Inputs to $R_t$, an $R_t$ layer,
  observation layers, and multiple data streams
- Not seen this used in research yet. Proposed in Samuel Brand's
  `RenewalExamples` repository

::: {.attribution}
Pervez, Locatello and Gavves 2024, *Mechanistic Neural Networks*,
[arXiv:2402.13077](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13077) ·
[github.com/SamuelBrand1/RenewalExamples][rex] · the 2026 Wellcome
Discovery application
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/exchange-renewal-layer.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="On the left the renewal equation, I_t equals R_t times the sum
over s of I_{t minus s} g_s, described as a convolution with a fixed
kernel scaled by R_t. On the right a stack of six layers: inputs, an R_t
layer marked learned, then a renewal layer, a delay layer and an
ascertainment layer marked fixed by the epidemiology, then a negative
binomial likelihood on each stream."}

::: {.attribution}
Drawn for this talk, `scripts/exchange-schematics.py`
:::
:::

## An outbreak-specific foundation model {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **Time series foundation models.** Pretrained on many series from
  other domains. Your series in, a forecast out, no fitting
- Good a few weeks out on sparse data. Less good at peaks and turning
  points
- **CAPE** pretrains on simulated compartmental epidemics. A model of
  outbreaks, but of the final curves
- **Outbreak data change after the fact.** On the DRC model the daily
  suspected stream stopped on 6 August. In May INSP, the DRC's public
  health institute, reclassified suspected cases
- How do these methods hold up when the data change under them, in
  prospective settings?

::: {.attribution}
Kalahasti et al. 2025, medRxiv · Wang, Li and Perra 2026, medRxiv ·
Jafari et al. 2026, [arXiv:2606.19560](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19560)
· Liu et al. 2026, CAPE, KDD · PNAS 2026,
[doi:10.1073/pnas.2526192123](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2526192123) ·
[BVDOutbreakSize][bvd] `README.md`
:::
:::
